curated.notes: Aristocrats go-wide: Caesar sacrifices an attacker-adjacent creature on attack for tokens, cards or damage, so the deck wants to attack every turn with a wide board and keep token makers running (Assemble the Legion, Bastion of Remembrance, Pitiless Plunderer, Skullclamp). PLAY_AGGRO and always-on token abilities are the heuristic levers; Forge's ARISTOCRATS strategy is detected from the commander text on its own. No tutors in the list, so key cards act as discard protection and Monte Carlo plan pieces.
curated.by: hand, from the decklist and Forge's plan detectors (DESIGN.md §19)

playbook.notes: Version 4 = the shipped version 3 (its attack, its trigger rule and its six cast rules, unchanged and in their order: now rules 12 to 17) with eleven rules in front for the deck's board wipes, which version 3 left to Forge. Written from the 200 games of the bot league (league-run #2, seed 20261190), where the seat lost 168. Drawn and cast there: Ruinous Ultimatum 35 and 7, Martial Coup 41 and 11 (ten of the eleven for X of one to four, the wipe once), Hour of Reckoning 34 and 9, Vault 75 38 and 16 (Caesar exiled by it in 13 of the 16), The Nipton Lottery 33 and 8. With one of them in hand on its last own turn of a loss the seat had three or four creatures and 8 to 17 life against ten to fourteen creatures, Token Triumph's in 11 or 12 losses of about 20. Rules 1-2, Ruinous Ultimatum (one-sided): as soon as it can be paid for and an opponent has four creatures or could hit for 12. Its cost is the limit, not the rule: with the card in hand and seven lands RRWWWBB was there on 35 of 63 turns. Rule 3, the emergency: an opponent could kill us next turn (threat >= life) with more power than we have, and we have four creatures or fewer: Martial Coup for X of five or more, else The Nipton Lottery, else Vault 75, else Hour of Reckoning. 'Four or fewer' is from the league: a lethal threat from a stronger board stood on some own turn in 86% of the seat's losses and 84% of its wins, and with four creatures or fewer of ours in 68% and 31%. Rule 4: the same (without Hour of Reckoning, which leaves tokens) against 50 power or more whatever our own board: a local game was lost to 106 power with Martial Coup in hand and six creatures of ours. Rule 5: the two full wipes before it is lethal, at 20 power, with four creatures or fewer: by the league's logs that moves Martial Coup from a median of 10 life at the cast to 24, and the local emergency casts, at 10 and 11 life, bought turns and no wins. Not seen to fire locally. Rule 6: Martial Coup with one creature or none of ours (five Soldiers for it) once an opponent has five. Not seen to fire locally. Rules 7-8, Vault 75 (chapter I exiles power 4 or more, Caesar included): at 20 with Caesar off the battlefield, at 25 with him on it; they stand before Caesar's own rule, so he is cast after chapter I. Local casts at 25: seven, six, eleven and five opposing creatures for three, one, two and one of ours; below 25: three, three, one and none. Rules 9-10, Hour of Reckoning as a play of its own when it costs little: Caesar off the battlefield and two creatures or fewer of ours, or nothing but tokens, and an opponent with five (local casts: four, nine and twelve opposing creatures for two, none and none; the one that cost Caesar left the seat no better off and the rule was narrowed). Rule 11 holds Martial Coup and Vault 75 for the rules above (Forge cast the Coup for a few Soldiers and the Vault into its own Caesar). The thresholds on threat were set on estimates from the logs (base power, or what a creature of that name last hit for); the engine's own numbers run higher. Left to Forge as before: V.A.T.S., Lethal Scheme, Anguished Unmaking, Wear // Tear (cast in 87 to 98% of the games they are drawn, aimed by Forge's own logic) and Entrapment Maneuver (an instant for an opponent's attack: no rule reaches it). Local tables of bots, seed 20269010, too few games to measure anything: tables 1-10 under a first version of these rules 5 wins of 10; tables 11-20 under these rules 1 of 10, where the shipped playbook also won 1 of 10 and the seat under these rules lasted 1.4 own turns longer and took 17 less damage a game. A candidate: not played at 200 tables. Shipped on 2026-11-12 as version 4: at 200 tables of bots (ab-run #21 joined with #20, seed 20261200) 55 wins against version 3's 36 on the same tables (+9.5 points, 95% +5 to +14, 23 discordant pairs against 4, exact test 0.0003) and the stock pilot's 25. Version 5 (2026-11-12): the attack is left to Forge. Measured on version 3's rules (ab-run #23 joined with #20, seed 20261200): 41 wins with Forge's own attack against 36 with the go-wide attack (+2.5 points, 95% -4 to +9, exact test 0.53) and the stock pilot's 25. Version 4's answer rules and Forge's attack have not been played together yet: that is the next round. Version 6 (2026-11-13) puts the go-wide attack back. On the first round on the pool of twelve (ab-run #26, seed 20261240, DESIGN §28) these same rules won 66 of 200 tables with the go-wide attack against 45 with the attack left to Forge (+10.5 points, 95% +4 to +17, 36 discordant pairs against 15, exact test 0.0046) and the stock pilot's 28. The 66 is the better of two arms on the same tables, so it is flattered by the choosing; the next run on tables of its own is the figure for this version.
